d: RopeConstraint prevents two attachments from separating further than a defined length, with optional behavior as an extending or contracting winch.
h:
For an overview on creating, visualizing, and simulating mechanical constraints, including RopeConstraint, see Mechanical constraints. Also see Roblox units to understand how Roblox units compare to metric units.

A RopeConstraint prevents two attachments from separating further than a defined Length. The attachments can move closer together than this length and both can freely rotate. Restitution defines the elasticity of the attachments when they reach the separation limit specified by Length.

This constraint can also be powered to behave as a motorized winch.

Winch

If a rope's WinchEnabled property is enabled, it attempts to translate the attachments to a set separation specified by WinchTarget, effectively the target length of the rope in studs. This translation is controlled by WinchSpeed, WinchResponsiveness, and WinchForce.

WinchSpeed must be a positive value, used to either contract or extend the rope length to WinchTarget. Setting a negative speed will revert to 0, not reverse the winch servo direction.

kid.simple: A RopeConstraint works like a real rope between two attachments: they can come closer together, but they can never get farther apart than the rope's length. Both ends can spin freely. You can also turn it into a winch that reels the rope in or out to a target length. Ropes are great for swings, grappling hooks, cranes and hanging bridges.
kid.analogy: A dog on a leash: the dog can run right up to you, but once the leash is tight it cannot go any farther. A winch is like a fishing reel that winds the line in.
keyPoints: A rope stops two attachments from separating more than its `Length` in studs.
The attachments can move closer than the Length, and both can rotate freely.
`Restitution` sets how bouncy it is when the rope snaps tight.
Turn on `WinchEnabled` to make it a motorized winch that changes the rope length to `WinchTarget`.
`WinchSpeed`, `WinchResponsiveness` and `WinchForce` control how fast and how strongly the winch reels.
`WinchSpeed` must be positive. A negative speed becomes 0; it does not reverse the winch. To reel out, raise `WinchTarget` instead.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (0, 3, 0) sits 3 studs above the center of its part.
terms.Length: The longest the rope can be. With Length 10, the attachments can be 0 to 10 studs apart, never 11.
terms.CurrentDistance: A read-only property telling you how far apart the attachments are right now.
terms.restitution: How bouncy the rope is when it goes tight. 0 means it stops dead; 1 means it bounces back as hard as it hit.
terms.winch: A motor that winds a rope in or lets it out, like on a crane or tow truck.
terms.WinchTarget: The rope length, in studs, the winch is trying to reach.
terms.WinchSpeed: How fast the winch changes the length, in studs per second. Going from 10 to 3 at speed 2 takes (10 - 3) / 2 = 3.5 seconds.
terms.WinchForce: How strong the winch is. To lift something, it must be stronger than the object's weight (mass x 196.2).
terms.WinchResponsiveness: How sharply the winch reacts. Higher values are snappier.

example.title: A crane that lifts a crate with a winch
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local arm = Instance.new("Part")
arm.Size = Vector3.new(2, 1, 2)
arm.Position = Vector3.new(0, 20, -20)
arm.Anchored = true
arm.Parent = Workspace

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Size = Vector3.new(3, 3, 3)   -- volume 27, Wood density 0.35: mass about 9.45
crate.Material = Enum.Material.Wood
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 1.5, -20)
crate.Parent = Workspace

local armAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
armAtt.Position = Vector3.new(0, -0.5, 0)   -- bottom of the arm (height 19.5)
armAtt.Parent = arm

local crateAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
crateAtt.Position = Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0)  -- top of the crate (height 3)
crateAtt.Parent = crate

local rope = Instance.new("RopeConstraint")
rope.Attachment0 = armAtt
rope.Attachment1 = crateAtt
rope.Length = 17           -- just enough to reach: 19.5 - 3 = 16.5
rope.Visible = true
rope.WinchEnabled = true
rope.WinchTarget = 17      -- start at full length (crate on the ground)
rope.WinchSpeed = 2        -- studs per second
rope.WinchForce = 10000    -- crate weighs about 9.45 x 196.2 = 1854
rope.Parent = arm

task.wait(2)
rope.WinchTarget = 4       -- reel in: 17 - 4 = 13 studs at 2 per second = 6.5 seconds
task.wait(10)
rope.WinchTarget = 17      -- lower it again
explain: The arm is anchored 20 studs up. The rope runs from the arm's bottom (19.5) to the crate's top (3), a gap of 16.5 studs, so a Length of 17 has a little slack.
`WinchEnabled = true` turns the rope into a winch. At first `WinchTarget` is 17, so nothing changes.
When `WinchTarget` drops to 4, the winch reels in 13 studs. At `WinchSpeed = 2` that takes about 6.5 seconds, lifting the crate.
The crate is Wood: 27 cubic studs x 0.35 density = mass 9.45, so it weighs about 1854. A `WinchForce` of 10000 is plenty.
Setting `WinchTarget` back to 17 lets the rope out and lowers the crate.

watchOut: A rope does not push. If you need two things to stay an exact distance apart, use a RodConstraint instead.
If the winch cannot lift something, `WinchForce` is too low compared to its weight.
Setting `WinchSpeed` to a negative number does not reverse it. It just becomes 0. Change `WinchTarget` to reel the other way.
Ropes are invisible unless you set `Visible = true`.
